rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is nonexistent, so the first experiment should test a baseline multimodal configuration to evaluate whether combining RNA and image data improves performance. This configuration uses PCA and ResNet50 encoders with simple concatenation fusion, which is a logical starting point to assess the impact of multimodal integration. It clarifies whether multimodal approaches are worth pursuing before exploring more complex designs.

The existing evidence shows that config_016 (multimodal, concat fusion) achieves 0.526 validation accuracy. This experiment tests whether switching to weighted fusion (config_017) improves performance, clarifying the impact of fusion strategy. It directly addresses a key design choice (fusion method) with minimal changes, balancing exploitation of the multimodal direction and exploration of critical components.

Existing evidence shows that for singleprofile multimodal models with pca_n2000 and resnet50, concat fusion slightly outperforms weighted fusion. This experiment tests the same RNA/image encoders but with multiprofile and avgpool aggregation, clarifying whether profile setting and aggregation method are critical factors. It balances exploration of key design choices (profile setting) with exploitation of proven components (pca_n2000/resnet50).

Existing evidence shows that multimodal multiprofile configurations with pca_n2000 and resnet50 encoders achieve high accuracy (0.6186) when using avgpool aggregation and concat fusion (config_018). This experiment tests whether switching to weighted fusion (config_019) could further improve performance, clarifying whether fusion method matters for multiprofile tasks. It builds on the strong foundation of config_018 while exploring a key design choice with potential impact.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (e.g., config_019) achieve high accuracy (0.639). This experiment tests replacing the image encoder (resnet50 → imagenet_vit_l) in this high-performing setup to evaluate whether a more advanced image encoder further improves performance. This clarifies the impact of image encoder choice, a critical design decision, while maintaining other successful components, balancing exploitation of the current baseline with exploration of key hyperparameters.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (e.g., config_019) achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.639). This experiment tests whether switching aggregation from avgpool to transformer (a more complex method) further improves performance, clarifying the importance of aggregation strategy. It is the best next step as it directly builds on the current top-performing configuration while exploring a critical design decision with potential for significant impact.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile, pca_n2000 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_019) achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.638999). This experiment tests whether using the more advanced imagenet_vit_l image encoder with transformer aggregation (instead of avgpool) and weighted fusion could further improve performance. This clarifies the impact of image encoder complexity and aggregation method, both critical design choices, while building on the promising direction of weighted fusion.

The existing evidence shows config_019 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) achieves the highest validation accuracy (0.639). This experiment tests transformer aggregation with the same RNA and image encoders, clarifying whether transformer aggregation improves performance compared to avgpool. It directly extends the top-performing configuration, balancing exploitation of proven components with exploration of aggregation methods.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile, avgpool, and weighted fusion with resnet50 image encoder achieve high accuracy (config_019: 0.639). This experiment tests whether replacing pca_n2000 with scvi_n200 RNA encoder (a more sophisticated model) maintains or improves performance, clarifying the importance of RNA encoder choice. It is the best next step as it directly addresses a key design decision with potential for significant impact.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_031) achieve the highest accuracy (0.6776). This experiment tests whether replacing the image encoder with imagenet_vit_l (a more advanced model) and switching aggregation to transformer (which may better handle multiprofile data) could further improve performance. This clarifies the impact of image encoder quality and aggregation method on accuracy, balancing exploration of promising components with exploitation of existing strong results.
